issue: Survival does not shape the gene loadings F; the fitted model behaves as matrix factorization followed by Cox.
diagnosis: Reconstruction precision sums over n×p entries and Cox over the events, so survival supplies 10^-6 to 10^-4 of the loading precision on real data. Weighting survival up to an equal share (about 10^4) breaks convergence in the current code.
solution: Scale the Cox working weights by a balance factor γ and add the pieces that should keep a strongly weighted fit stable: damping, a non-collapsing β prior, a survival-informed start, sparse nonnegative priors.
status: in progress: single-weight test done (no single weight works in the current code); new fitter next
source: spec 1; code review closing question; derivation comparison

issue: The earlier survival term in the F update updated all genes at once and omitted the coupling between genes of the same program.
diagnosis: Every correlated gene regressed the full residual onto itself, overshooting the predictor and causing runaway feedback between L and F.
solution: Gene-by-gene (Gauss–Seidel) update with the coupling term and the projection refreshed after each gene, with precision damping.
status: partly done: the canonical path already has the coupled update; damping is new

issue: A low-variance prognostic program never gets a nonzero coefficient, so survival never pulls a factor toward it.
diagnosis: The survival gradient on F_k is multiplied by β_k. A start from the top SVD directions misses the program, so β_k ≈ 0 and the gradient is zero.
solution: Hybrid start: K−2 factors from NMF/SVD plus two columns from the positive and negative parts of the univariate Cox score, then a short β warm-up.

issue: Survival coefficients collapse to exactly zero on real multimodal data and in some CV folds, and then stay there.
diagnosis: Both current β priors have an absorbing zero: the per-factor Normal variance estimate hits 0 when |x/s| ≤ 1, and the shared point-Laplace slab weight can hit 0 when only one of K factors is prognostic.
solution: Point-normal prior on β with the slab proportion bounded to [1/K, 0.5] and a minimum slab scale.

issue: Joint expression and methylation fits hit the sweep cap without converging.
diagnosis: Rescaling each factor by a data-dependent SD changes the next sweep's precisions; the β prior is not carried through rescaling; KL values were cached out of sync with the prior.
solution: Rescale L to unit RMS with the exact inverse map on F; normalize F inside the predictor so β never needs rescaling; compute KL directly from each ebnm result.

issue: The ELBO counted the Gaussian log-normalizer of the L update once instead of once per patient.
diagnosis: A helper summed over the length of the precision vector, which is 1 for the L update.
solution: Replicate the scalar precision before summing; test against the exact KL.
status: done: fixed and tested; the benchmark rerun shows unchanged external C and better convergence (5 of 5 CV folds, against 2 of 5)

issue: Exponential priors without a point mass at zero never prune; post-hoc deletion either deletes nothing (multimodal) or rotates the prognostic program away (single block).
diagnosis: Exponential priors have no mass at zero. Deleting a factor while holding the rest frozen is dominated by the reconstruction term; refitting at K−1 lets the protected program absorb the deleted variance.
solution: Point-exponential priors on L and F; no deletion refits; report survival-active, genomics-only and inactive factors from the fitted K; choose K and the supervision strength by training CV with the one-SE rule.

issue: Methylation dominates expression, and adding CpGs destabilizes the fit (predictor SD in the tens of thousands at 25,000 CpGs).
diagnosis: Projection and precisions are unnormalized sums over features, so the block with more features dominates.
solution: Weight each block by its feature count and scale each block's projection by 1/(M√p_m); make log-space risk sets and a curvature floor the default.

issue: Single-block and multimodal models differ: z-scored data with nonnegative factors in one, intercepts and signed loadings in the other.
diagnosis: Z-scoring creates negative values that LF^T ≥ 0 cannot reconstruct; the multimodal model abandoned nonnegativity instead.
solution: One model with M = 1 as the single-block case: divide each feature by its within-cohort SD without centering (Y ≥ 0), and center only inside the Cox projection.

issue: Dense projections dilute the survival signal at large p; survival pre-screening undercuts the method's claim.
diagnosis: Projecting thousands of background genes adds noise; screening on survival first means the factorization no longer discovers the prognostic program.
solution: Keep the unsupervised mean/variance screen as primary; survival screening only as an ablation; report a feature-count sensitivity curve.

issue: Pooling cohorts without per-cohort scaling collapses β; a cohort indicator column in L lowers external C.
diagnosis: Unscaled pooling makes the top factor a between-cohort technical difference; the indicator wastes a factor.
solution: Scale within cohort; no indicator column; stratified Cox risk sets and per-cohort residual precisions where needed.

issue: Comparator scripts chose each cohort's risk direction from validation outcomes (max(C, 1−C)).
diagnosis: This uses the outcome being evaluated and biases null C upward.
solution: Fix the direction once from the training fit.
status: done: fixed; rescoring the saved risks changes none of the 20 comparator values

issue: Three RNA-seq cohorts were log-transformed twice.
diagnosis: The cohort loader and the preprocessing step both applied log2(x+1).
solution: Log once; test each cohort's scale against its setting.
status: done: fixed and tested; external C unchanged (mean 0.625 vs 0.627)

issue: PACA-AU donors appear in two external series (47 shared donors plus one duplicate), so pooled intervals resample records rather than donors.
diagnosis: 568 unique donors across 616 records.
solution: One record per donor in pooled analyses, donor-level or cohort-stratified bootstrap.

issue: Four tests read baselines from a local branch and failed for anyone else.
diagnosis: The tests called git on a branch that is not pushed in that form.
solution: Store the baselines as test fixtures.

issue: The pre-registered supervision test (ΔC = −0.003, 95% CI −0.029 to 0.024) is not reported, and the summary leads with a comparison against a 40-factor two-step model instead of the matched K = 7 one.
diagnosis: Reporting lagged the analysis.
solution: Report the null result; lead with the matched comparison (+0.011, −0.013 to 0.033); list every use of the external cohorts.

issue: Missing comparators and a writeup with hand-typed numbers.
diagnosis: Comparators deferred; writeup has no executed code.
solution: Add PurIST as a prognostic comparator, DeSurv head to head, elastic-net Cox and clinical covariates; compute every number and figure from saved results.

issue: The single-block risk score may carry the opposite sign to the documented hazard convention.
diagnosis: A post-fit global flip based on training C can override the sign the partial likelihood chose.
solution: Check the saved benchmark fit; fix or document the convention.

issue: Stored β variances may be zero where the derivation implies they are positive.
diagnosis: To be checked against the saved fit.
solution: Store Var(β) + E[β]^2 consistently and add a test.

issue: One test collapses to an all-zero fit on Linux with reference BLAS.
diagnosis: An all-zero ebnm return looks converged.
solution: Not pursued, since all work runs locally; the new fitter must flag an all-zero fit as a failure.
